content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation on § 10.3 (p0063), preferred-level redline validated (`ok:true`).**

**What I checked**
- § 10.3 is the only assignment provision anywhere in the Agreement. Searches for "assign", "transfer", "consent", "change of control", and a regex for merger/acquisition/substantially all/affiliate/subsidiary surfaced nothing else.
- § 4.1 (term/termination on 90 days' notice), § 4.2 (Termination Payment) and § 1.6 contain **no** change-of-control trigger or re-pricing right — so we are not in walk-away territory, but the protection is unstated rather than granted.
- § 6.1/6.3 exclusivity names Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled as competitors, and §§ 6.1, 7.1 and 8 give HDI our Marks licence, customer e-mail list access and Confidential Information — which is why unrestricted HDI assignability is materially adverse to us.

**Why it fails the fallback (not merely short of preferred)**
The clause is pure boilerplate — successors and assigns are bound, but there is no assignment right, no written-notice mechanic, no consent gate for other assignments and no reasonableness standard. Three of the four fallback elements are absent, and the practical effect is a one-way risk: HDI could transfer the hosting relationship to a competitor without asking us.

**The change**
A single inserted sentence group after the existing § 10.3 text (existing sentence preserved intact) carrying all six preferred elements: Company assignment to an affiliate or M&A successor without consent; HDI assignment only with our consent, not unreasonably withheld; never to a Company competitor; and no HDI termination right on a change of control of the Company. The mutual notice-only fallback is offered in the comment if HDI resists the competitor bar.
